stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: Fever-Aces Game 3 live analysis and top plays
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Indiana on Thursday with the winner advancing to the WNBA semifinals. We're live courtside.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Two spots in the WNBA semifinals remain open, but one will be claimed Thursday. The No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces, the WNBA's defending champions, host the No. 6 seed Indiana Fever in a decisive Game 3.

After the Fever's 99-89 win over the Aces on Tuesday in Indianapolis evened their first-round series 1-1, the teams meet to determine which team advances past the first round. The Aces have won three of the past four championships. The Fever's lone title came in 2012.

Emotions will run high at Michelob Ultra Arena. On Tuesday in Indianapolis, Aces star A'ja Wilson objected to a fan pointing at her from behind the basket and left the court to confront him. The WNBA rulebook bars players or coaches from going into the stands to confront spectators. But on Thursday, the league announced there would be no further discipline for Wilson or any other Aces involved in the incident.

We broke down what might decide which team moves on, and now ESPN's Kareem Copeland and Michael Voepel are courtside for live analysis, updates and highlights.

JUMP TO: Keys to the game | Live coverage from Las Vegas

Can the Fever replicate Tuesday's defense?

During the regular season, the Fever ranked ninth in defensive rating (estimate of points allowed per 100 possessions) at 110.3, and the Aces were fifth (107.2). Las Vegas was better on both ends of the court in Game 1, and Indiana knew it had to improve its defense Tuesday to keep its season going.

The Fever did that, at times frustrating all the Aces except Jackie Young, whom they could not stop (31 points). The Aces still scored 89 points. But during both the second and third quarters, the Fever held the Aces to 17 points.

That put Indiana in the driver's seat for the fourth quarter. The Aces made a run, outscoring the Fever 29-27 in the final period, but the middle-game defense gave Indiana enough cushion.

"I thought we played with a back-against-the-wall desperation that you need to play with at playoff time," Indiana coach Stephanie White said.

Now they need to do that again.

How well will Wilson play?

It's rare to see Wilson lose her cool, but on Tuesday the Fever defense seemed to frustrate her at times. She was 5-of-11 from the field but 12-of-13 from the line. Wilson was the WNBA's leading scorer in the regular season and is one of the most clutch players in league history. That latter trait could make all the difference in Game 3.

Coach Becky Hammon thought defense was the Aces' biggest problem in Game 2. She said that kept them from being the offensive team they normally are, and that impacted Wilson's performance.

"I thought [the Fever] brought a lot of congestion [in the lane]," Hammon said. "Them picking up, being disruptive, got us out of our flow a little bit. At times, your offense has to help your defense. I thought defensively we were poor tonight, and the two are married together. We know when we're a good defensive team, we become very elite offensively."

Can the Fever guards do enough for a victory?

The backcourt of Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell has been one of the most entertaining shows in the WNBA all season, and it was outstanding Tuesday. Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds. Mitchell had 26 points.

The Fever also got strong defense from two other guards: starter Lexie Hull and reserve rookie Raven Johnson. Their energy was a big part of what helped the Fever rally and then take the lead after trailing 26-18 after the first quarter.

If the guards do their job, the Fever are formidable. But post player Aliyah Boston ultimately could be the difference-maker. She came back after a tough first quarter Tuesday and had 22 points. That was her highest scoring output since also getting 22 on Aug. 22.

Can Indiana slow down Jackie Young?

Young has 52 points and 15 assists through two games of this series. Like her teammates Wilson and Chelsea Gray, Young is a seasoned big-game player. That trio has won three WNBA championships together. And while Wilson is the perennial MVP candidate and Gray is the "Point Gawd," Young also has been indispensable for Las Vegas since being drafted No. 1 in 2019.

Wilson, Young and Gray are Hall of Fame-level players. But the Aces got nine points and five rebounds from starter Stephanie Talbot, too, and that's significant. Jewell Loyd and Cheyenne Parker-Tyus also can provide an offensive boost off the bench to back up the Aces' big three.

stories.headline: How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict
stories.summary: As the reaction to Man City's guilty verdict continues to ripple across the sporting world, the club's internal messaging is very much one of confidence and carrying on. That may be easier said than done.
stories.body:
The strength of the judgment against Manchester City, following their legal case with the Premier League, has shocked the club, its employees and their players. Most of those inside the City Football Academy (CFA) accept that the verdict -- made public for the first time Tuesday -- is a worst-case scenario.

There has been speculation and discussion on and off at the CFA for more than three years since the charges were announced in February 2023 about what might happen. It was always viewed internally as highly unlikely that every count of financial misconduct would be proved.

City insist they are innocent -- a message that has come from the top, namely chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano -- and many employees want to give the club the benefit of the doubt. They enjoy working for City and feel that they've been well looked after over the years.

In that respect, many people ESPN spoke with for this story are choosing to believe Al Mubarak and Soriano. At the very least, the majority of these staff members are prepared to wait until after the appeal is heard before passing judgment.

- Legal explainer: Man City have been charged. Now what?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City come back from seismic scandal

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict ruin Guardiola's legacy?

Many staff members are also fans, and as such, they are invested personally as well as professionally. City are a big club and a major employer, but since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, the club's owners have done a good job of creating a family feel and a sense of shared purpose. More than 700 employees attended a UK all-staff meeting in the first week of this three-week international break, while players are away on duty with their national teams.

There is, however, a cloud hanging over the CFA, and the mood in general has been described to ESPN as nervous. Soriano, in his video message to staff Tuesday, insisted it should be business as usual, but in the absence of any real information about what sanctions might follow, there's genuine worry about what the future could hold.

The same goes for the players. With many of City's senior squad away on international duty, some have had direct contact with the club, while others have not. One agent of a first-team player told ESPN that his client is "calm" about the situation and is happy with the public reassurances offered by senior executives. There is, though, an acceptance that things could change depending on the result of the appeal -- which has yet to be filed but must be lodged by the close of business Friday -- and any punishment handed down.

Player concerns

Speculation over considerable sporting sanctions is causing the most concern, sources tell ESPN. After all, City's players chose to go to the Etihad Stadium to play in the Premier League and the Champions League while getting the opportunity to win trophies. They need to be playing well at the highest level to earn international call-ups and to play at major international tournaments.

For that reason, one representative of a City first-teamer has privately questioned the sense in punishing current players who were not at the club when the alleged transgressions occurred between 2009 and 2018. Another agent has told ESPN that the players -- many of whom arrived or penned new deals after February 2023, when the charges were first announced -- knew what they were signing up for because possible punishments have been widely known for a while.

Sources have told ESPN that the Professional Football Association (PFA) has made itself available to talk to players about issues arising from the verdict. It helped a number of players at the end of last season when Southampton were expelled from the playoffs because a staff member was caught spying on opponents' training sessions; in that case, a significant sporting sanction was handed down for an incident that didn't involve the team but did directly impact them.

It's unclear how many City players have clauses in their contracts to protect themselves in the event of relegation, or a points deduction so severe that it prevents the club from challenging for the title or playing in Europe for a number of years. "There may be a few tough lessons for players whose agents focus purely on how much their client is paid," one agent told ESPN.

Sources have told ESPN that other clubs are monitoring City's situation carefully and work is already going on in the background to find out what protections -- if any -- players have in their contracts, and whether or not they are accessible for transfer talks. Questions are also being asked privately about whether there's an appetite -- even at this early stage -- to consider alternative options away from the Etihad in the future.

The football department is keen to minimize any distractions. Manager Enzo Maresca is expected to address the verdict when his players return to the CFA next week, and his message is likely to center on a need to remain focused on football.

Whether that's possible or not is another matter. The story has already followed City's players wherever they've played during the international break. Norway manager Stale Solbakken was asked about Erling Haaland's mindset ahead of Norway's game against Wales in Cardiff. "Everything is fine," he said. Rúben Dias, stern-faced, shut down a question at a Portugal news conference.

Manchester City women's manager Andree Jeglertz became the first City employee to take questions about the Premier League verdict at a news conference Wednesday, held to preview their game against Real Madrid. "The thing the club has been presented is the information we have inside of our group," he said.

"We can't talk about anything else and we don't need to talk about anything else at the moment."

It's likely to be a similar message when Maresca sits down with reporters for the first time next week. He's due to speak at his next scheduled news conference on Oct. 9, two days before the trip to play Liverpool at Anfield.

Through the lens of the Premier League's statement, this next fixture has taken on added intensity and spice given Liverpool have finished second behind City three times in the past 15 years. Of all the clubs who feel most wronged by all this, Liverpool are close to the top of the list.

Amid all the noise, Man City have told their staff to plow on. That may be easier said than done.

stories.headline: 76ers envision LeBron James' role being 'offense creator'
stories.summary: Sixers coach Nick Nurse envisions LeBron James setting the table for the offense this season. "I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- It took until Day 3 of training camp for Philadelphia 76ers coach Nick Nurse to introduce offensive schemes to his new group.

And though the offense flowed with expected ease Thursday during 5-on-0 drills, role definition will be as important as understanding the playbook when the real games start.

Nurse detailed the offensive responsibilities he envisions LeBron James occupying. The team will certainly put the ball in the 24-year veteran's capable hands -- as, team sources told ESPN, Philadelphia discussed playing James at point forward this offseason -- but he won't be the only one with the ball.

"We got several guys that what I would call 'grab-and-go,'" Nurse said. "If they get rebounds and their first advantage is to start pushing it up the floor and it stays that way, then they're going to do it."

Beyond James, the group Nurse will rely on to push the team in transition includes fellow starters Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Though Nurse emphasized defense during the first two days of camp, part of the presentation was imploring his players to get stops to spark fast-break opportunities when scoring will come instinctively.

When the Sixers set up in the half court, however, Nurse is glad to have James, who ranks No. 1 in all-time points and No. 4 in all-time assists on this team.

"I just think LeBron, I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said. "I don't necessarily mean scorer, I just think creator and a table setter and all that kind of stuff. ... If it isn't bringing it up and starting [the possession], it's probably going to be first pass anyway to [him on] the wing and then we get into our actions, and he's kind of seeing what's there, and he's creating offense for others."

As the Sixers look to organize themselves against a set defense, that's when player recognition will be paramount.

James, Brown and Joel Embiid, for instance, can operate out of the post to initiate offense. The court, however, can get awfully crowded if the team has a player planted on either block and any of those three expect their touches there.

"One, it's a feel thing, and two, we just try to establish some spacing," Brown said. "We try to establish position on the floor, like the style of play. I think we're still kind of figuring it out. Like when I am going to go, when not to go, when big fella is going down in the post, when I can put pressure on the rim, just trying to find that balance."

Brown has already spent time with coaches after practice this week, not only practicing fadeaway shots when double-teamed in the post, but also practicing throwing passes to the 3-point line to elude the double.

Sixers player development coaches have been the recipients of those passes, but the idea is for Brown to picture finding one of his star teammates open if he dissects the defense properly.

"I played with a fair share of stretch 5s, and it really complements my game well," Brown said of Embiid.

Just like how Nurse welcomes James' input to complement his coaching.

"I would like to have a collaborative situation here," Nurse said. "So, when just about anything that's on the table, he can say, 'What are you thinking about doing?' Any thoughts. Any ideas. And not just with him. I actually did it with five of the players this morning before practice."

There will be only a couple of more practice opportunities before the Sixers' offense will see a real opposing defense. Philadelphia's preseason opener is scheduled for Monday against the New York Knicks.

stories.headline: NHL's Gary Bettman monitoring how no-trade clauses are used
stories.summary: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman believes that no-trade clauses are no longer being used as "originally intended," and instead, players are using them to force moves to specific teams after requesting a trade.
stories.body:
NHL commissioner Gary Bettman believes that no-trade clauses are no longer being used as "originally intended," and instead, players are using them to force moves to specific teams after requesting a trade.

"As I look at what's happening now, I don't think that's a good thing. I don't think it's good for the player, the club or the fans' connection to the game," said Bettman in an interview with Sportsnet 590 in Toronto on Thursday.

Bettman said that trade protection was originally put in place to protect players from teams trading them after signing a long-term contract.

"Maybe you're giving a hometown discount, and you wanted to make sure you can be where you wanted to be, and where you're signing up to be," said Bettman.

Several high-profile NHL players who recently sought a change in scenery have used their no-movement or no-trade clauses to control their next destinations:

The Ottawa Senators said that captain Brady Tkachuk used his no-movement clause to force a trade to the Florida Panthers last summer, where his brother Matthew plays.
Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski reportedly told the team he wouldn't sign a new contract when his deal is up in 2028 and then blocked a trade to the Dallas Stars.
Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin asked for a trade but narrowed the field of trade partners to just three teams.
Winnipeg Jets star goalie Connor Hellebuyck also has a no-movement clause and was suspended by the team after failing to show up to training camp after requesting a trade.

"This notion now, where you can select where you want to go to and you can demand a trade, that was never the original intention," said Bettman. "If this becomes a problem -- I don't think one offseason a problem makes -- but if it becomes a problem, it's something we are going to have to discuss with the players' association."

The way no-trade clauses have been used has "flipped" in recent years, according to one player agent speaking to ESPN, as part of an overall player empowerment movement in the NHL.

"The players are taking it into their own hands," the agent said. "I don't exactly know when it changed, but it's a copycat league. And if you see somebody use it to that effect, and you have a player that's in that situation, you almost feel obligated to bring this idea to the table with them if they're unhappy with where they're at. Then it starts to become ubiquitous for the guys that have those clauses."

The NHL and NHLPA just saw their latest collective bargaining agreement kick in last month, and it runs until Sept. 15, 2030. Bettman said the league will be monitoring how trade protection is being utilized, going forward.

"While it might be good for a player in a particular case -- although based on what we're witnessing now, I'm not sure it's good for the player either -- we have to look at what's good for the game, the players overall and the league. It's something we're going to keep an eye on. I think we've gotten past the way no-trade clauses were originally intended," he said.

Others believe the responsibility for how these clauses are used ultimately falls on the teams and not the players.

"This is the biggest nonissue in the NHL," said player agent Allan Walsh in a recent tweet. "No one forces teams to give out no-move and no-trade clauses. They are freely negotiated as part of NHL contracts."

stories.headline: UFC 332 preview and picks: Why haven't there been more women's fights?
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 332 in Salt Lake City.
stories.body:
For all of the growth and progress of women's MMA over the past 15 years, the 2026 schedule has raised an uncomfortable -- but glaring -- question: What is happening to women's fights? Saturday's UFC 332 event in Salt Lake City will mark the first UFC event this year headlined by women, when Natalia Silva (20-5-1) and Wang Cong (10-1) meet for the vacant flyweight title. This year's lack of high-profile women's fights (and the excitement that should accompany them) has been impossible to miss. Wang, the 34-year-old Chinese challenger, has certainly felt it in the buildup to Saturday.

"Everyone was talking about how bad this main event is," Wang told ESPN, through an interpreter. "Of course I know about it. I think me and my opponent will prove them wrong, and show this is a fight they need to watch."

The sport could definitely use a boost. According to ESPN Research, the UFC has promoted 415 total bouts this year; 56 have featured women. That 13% split is the lowest mark in a decade.

The last women's fight to headline any UFC event was a non-title bout between Mackenzie Dern and Amanda Ribas in January 2025. For the last women's fight to headline a numbered event, one has to go all the way back to a bantamweight title fight between Amanda Nunes and Irene Aldana in June 2023.

Those trends are unlikely to change if some of the more underlying metrics continue to hold. Women's fights are increasingly being pushed to the prelims portion of events. In 2026, 83% of women's fights have appeared on prelims, compared with 72% in 2024, 61% in 2021 and 54% in 2017.

For their part, both Wang and Silva, a 29-year-old challenger out of Brazil, are predicting a memorable matchup Saturday. Wang is a former professional kickboxer with an aggressive style. Silva is known as more of a matador, but in 2024 when she went against Jessica Andrade, the most aggressive opponent of her UFC career, they won fight of the night.

"For sure, it's going to be a well-fought battle," Silva told ESPN through an interpreter. "She comes in aggressive, which gives me the opportunity to be aggressive as well. What I can tell people is that's going to be an incredible fight."

One thing is undeniable, Wang and Silva have a rare opportunity on Saturday to headline a numbered event with a women's title fight.

More storylines to watch
Gautier is getting the step up in competition he asked for
Ateba Gautier is an athletic, 24-year-old wrecking ball from Cameroon with a 5-0 record in the UFC that includes four knockouts. The combined record of his opponents, however, has been 4-14. That doesn't diminish what Gautier has done, but it's still unknown how he will fare against tougher competition.

For his part, Gautier isn't shying away from challenging himself. Immediately following his last win in May, Gautier called for a fight with former middleweight champion Israel Adesanya -- arguably the greatest 185-pound fighter of all time. The UFC didn't give him Adesanya, but he did get Roman Kopylov, a 35-year-old Russian with 12 UFC bouts. A win wouldn't validate Gautier as a title contender, but it would prove he's ready for greater tests.

Wint could be the sleeper breakout candidate of the card
In terms of fighters who can make an individual splash at UFC 332, Wang and Silva in the main event stand out. Payton Talbott taking on a former champion in Deiveson Figueiredo is an obvious one. Undefeated Jacobe Smith is a finishing machine, and the aforementioned Gautier is in the biggest fight of his career.

Quietly, Anthony Wint could steal the show. Wint's prelim fight against Lucas Armand will be his third in less than two months. He's a former collegiate and NFL linebacker, fighting out of a notoriously talented and striking-oriented gym in Kill Cliff FC. He already is very much on UFC CEO Dana White's radar, having earned his contract on "Contender Series" on Aug. 11. If he does something spectacular, expect White to give it attention in his postfight comments (which in turn, draws everyone's attention).

Coaches' questions for women's flyweight championship
'What is Natalia Silva's game plan under pressure?'

Cong's striking is on point. She is aggressive with it, but she makes mistakes with it as well. I feel like Silva is the more well-rounded fighter, and it's up to her to take advantage of that. If this fight does go to the ground, I think Silva will present bigger problems -- and I see that as a path to victory for her. Wang is going to look for the knockout, and because of that, she will overextend in certain positions. I have a gut feeling Silva is going to work some ground work into this one. Silva is so good at controlling the pace of a fight, but with Cong coming at her so aggressively, I think she'll be forced to try different stuff. It's a pick 'em fight. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Who will own the 'second exchange'?
Silva's path to victory is about space, timing and making Wang reset. Silva needs to use her movement and feints to keep Wang from getting comfortable and building combinations. Silva is best at range, not standing in the pocket. Her counters matter in this matchup. She doesn't just survive Wang's pressure, she scores with midrange kicks and southpaw counters after Wang overcommits. For Wang, it's about pressure without chasing. She needs to cut the cage. Containing Silva becomes the real job. This is where her low kick and body work become weapons. Silva's movement is a huge part of her defense. If Wang can consistently attack the legs and body, she can start shrinking the cage without simply chasing. Who controls what happens after the initial exchange? If Wang attacks, Silva counters and exits, that's Silva's fight. If Wang attacks, Silva tries to exit and Wang cuts her off, those are the moments Wang wants. Whoever imposes their will on that second exchange wins. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: Lando Norris urges F1 and social media giants to help tackle abuse after Franco Colapinto ban feud
stories.summary: Lando Norris called on Formula 1 and social media companies to do more to combat online abuse after the torrent of messages he received following last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Lando Norris called on Formula 1 and social media companies to do more to combat online abuse after the torrent of messages he received following last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The comment sections of Norris' social media channels were filled with thousands of negative and hateful messages after he said in a postrace interview that Alpine driver Franco Colapinto should be banned for causing the collision that took his McLaren out of the race.

Two days after the event in Baku, Norris publicly apologized for his postrace comments in a message shared with his 11.9 million followers on Instagram.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Norris explained why he made the apology and called on the sport, social media channels and drivers to do more to prevent extreme comments, including death threats.

"I said what I wanted to Franco, and he's the only one really that I need to share my opinion with and share my apology with," Norris said. "I don't need to do it on social media, and I don't feel like I need to use social media to do such a thing, but at the same time, there obviously was a lot of that noise and stuff in the background, and I thought it was only sensible to announce or show that I made that apology.

"But yeah, at the same time, I do still see social media at times, and I saw some bits, some not so good, some better, but sadly that's what we deal with. I think a lot of sports deal with [it], some of it's down to just passion, and that's what you always have in sports.

"I think you see a lot more of it because social media is such an easy thing to share your opinions on. And to a certain extent, I completely respect it, but obviously to the extent of online abuse, death threats, all those things, those are things that I think are way too far beyond being a fan of a sport, or a driver, or a person, or an athlete, whatever it is.

"There's a line, but it's not new, it's something that's been around every sport for a long time, and I think just highlights more the fact that social media platforms, sports, need to do more, and maybe the people, the drivers, athletes, whoever, more to stop this kind of stuff from happening, because some people can deal with it much better than others."

Norris said the reaction he received on social media would not stop him from speaking his mind, even though he regretted his postrace comments in Baku.

"I should never have said the sort of stuff that I said, so I get why some people might have been more unhappy, let's just say upset, which is understandable," he added.

"Obviously there's that line which was crossed at times, quite a lot, which is not just being upset at someone, this is much, much worse.

"But I think I'm always happy, in general, in speaking my mind, and saying if I like things, don't like things, if I agree with things or not. I know I'm not able to please everyone, and you're never going to have everyone on your side, so I think that's normal enough, that's life, and that's what you have to come around to accept at the end of the day."

- Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Colapinto accepted Norris' apology earlier this week, but on Thursday said he was surprised the McLaren driver chose to be so public with his criticism after the race.

"I think he was in the heat of the moment ... He knows what comments create because he suffered from it," Colapinto said.

"He was probably the driver that was speaking the most about hate a couple of years ago, just a few seasons ago. So I was very surprised. But then, of course, he apologised.

"Unfortunately, he also got a lot of hate from it. But I also felt it's a tricky situation with the outside world. And that's why I think we need to be a bit safe inside about the things we say. And I understand it in the heat of the moment to say things like that."

Colapinto's fanbase has proved particularly vocal online and as recently as the Spanish Grand Prix last month turned on his Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, with abuse that included messages sent to the Frenchman's family and girlfriend.

Asked what his message to those posting the negative comments online would be, Colapinto said: "My message is always the same, that they sometimes don't realise what you can create by writing in your keyword, and that we are humans, and it's not easy for us when we get these kind of things.

"I think it always goes to Argentinians, but we miss that it doesn't come only from Argentinians. It comes a lot from them, I fully agree. It doesn't just come from them, and they are extremely passionate, and they support me a lot. And it's bad, and they are bad many times, but it comes from all the world, and from many other fanbases.

"I don't know if we are not seeing it, I get loads of it and no one ever talks about it. I mean, it's fine because I don't look at social media too much. I don't go into it. But I know it affects a lot of people, and a lot of drivers, and a lot of families more than me.

"I hope that they improve. I've been asking for a long time. It's tricky for us drivers to control it. I think we are the ones to not do them more. But we are also really striving to improve the situation by ourselves. Because we try -- for me, it's been since last year that I've been talking about it. I am doing my best, but it's tricky."

In 2023 F1's governing body, the FIA, set up the United Against Online Abuse (UAOA) commission, which as recently as this year's British Grand Prix received the collective support of all 22 drivers in F1.

On its website, the UAOA says it "aims to design, develop and implement practical actions that can protect the integrity of sports across the world as safe and inclusive spaces for competitors, officials, journalists, and fans alike."

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Ivan: Nathan Cleary can get even better after Dally M
stories.summary: Ivan Cleary has spoken of the horror of watching his son Nathan's leg injury, and a belief he can still get better again after winning his first Dally M.
stories.body:
Ivan Cleary has admitted watching his son Nathan suffer a badly broken leg marked one of the hardest days of his career, feeling the line between father and coach blurred for the first time.

But the veteran Penrith mentor is insistent his son Nathan still has more levels to attain once he returns from his injury, following his landmark Dally M victory on Wednesday night.

Cleary's Dally M triumph completed the Penrith halfback's rugby league box set, having now claimed every major team and individual honour available to him by age 28.

Unable to attend in person after being released from hospital following emergency surgery on his leg, the Panthers halfback collected the game's top honour while in a wheelchair at home.

Coach Ivan also appeared emotional during Nathan's pre-recorded speech, after the trophy was hand-delivered to the halfback earlier in the day.

"His voice perked up from what it's been the past couple of days," Ivan told AAP.

"It's a pretty amazing award. You don't play the game for individual awards, but it's certainly nice to be recognised.

"Particularly this award, it's pretty much the No.1 award in the game."

Reminded that his son had now scaled virtually every possible mountain in the sport, the Penrith coach insisted there were still improvements left in his son's game.

"It's crazy," Ivan said.

"I know he'd say it and I probably think a bit the same. You don't reflect too much when it's still going on. But when you put it like that, it's amazing.

"But I know there is so much more to come as well, and I know he thinks that way as well."

Nathan has received positive early news from surgeons after the operation on his compound fracture and dislocated ankle, as a result of a hip-drop tackle in Sunday's preliminary-final loss to Newcastle.

He will soon undergo surgery on other foot after fighting through a broken bone to play the Knights, but Penrith are hopeful he will be right for round one in 2027.

"Sunday was definitely one of the harder days I have been through," coach Cleary said.

"It's the first time where the line of dad and coach got a bit blurred. And the loss, I guess we have had a lot of good days so you can't have it all your way.

"Very emotional, but life goes on."

Footage has also emerged of fullback Dylan Edwards not only being horrified by the graphic injury at first, but then also trying to stop Nathan from seeing it.

"I was just trying to keep him calm as I could," Edwards said.

"To his credit he is a tough person. And the way he was handling that was incredible.

"It was gut-wrenching, something you're not used to seeing on the footy field."

Edwards, meanwhile, is still hopeful of being able to represent Australia at the World Cup after avoiding knee surgery following a PCL injury in the loss.

"I'm not sure, I have to talk to Kevvie (coach Kevin Walters)," Edwards said, while wearing a brace at the Dally Ms.

stories.headline: Colts and Commanders try to build on Week 3 wins when they face each other in London
stories.summary: Last November, the Indianapolis Colts went to Europe and came home with an 8-2 record. They'd beaten Atlanta in Berlin and seemed on a glide...
stories.body:
Last November, the Indianapolis Colts went to Europe and came home with an 8-2 record. They'd beaten Atlanta in Berlin and seemed on a glide path to some sort of postseason berth.


It turned out to be their last victory of the season.


Before too long, quarterback Daniel Jones was hurt, and the bottom fell out during a seven-game skid. Now another international game is on Indy's schedule — this time in London against the Washington Commanders on Sunday.


“I think we try to keep these guys on a normal schedule,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said earlier this week. “So get the rest on the plane during the red-eye flight right there, and then we have a walkthrough Friday practice there. Don’t want to get out on the field right away, going on a long trip like that, and run those guys — because I’ve been a part of that where guys have stepped on the field Friday and gotten hamstrings.”


Both teams should be familiar with the challenges of playing overseas. Washington went to Spain last season and lost to Miami. Quarterback Jayden Daniels missed that game and was replaced by Marcus Mariota. The same could happen this year in London, but Daniels has been able to practice after missing last weekend's win over Seattle because of a dislocated elbow.


“Just taking it day by day,” he said Thursday, offering few hints about his likelihood of playing.


Both teams should feel as if they can take advantage of this matchup. The Colts (1-2) had to open the season with games against Baltimore, Kansas City and Houston. They took the Chiefs to overtime and then beat the Texans. Only one of their next five games is at home, however, so this neutral site matchup feels pivotal.


Washington (1-2) appeared to be in a dire situation when Daniels went down in Week 2, but Mariota led the Commanders to a victory over Seattle in their home opener last weekend. With Daniels on the mend and the Colts and New York Giants up next on the schedule, there's reason for newfound hope.


“Obviously Marcus means a lot. Grew up, and he hates when I say this, but grew up a fan of Marcus, obviously at Oregon and in Tennessee and stuff like that,” Daniels said. “But just being around him, just the type of person he is and how much he shows that he cares about me and wants me to be at my best and anything I need, he’s really out there for me.”


Need to know
Indianapolis (1-2) vs. Washington (1-2) in London.


When/where to watch: Sunday, 9:30 a.m. EDT, NFL Network.


Latest odds: Colts by 4.


Against the spread: Colts 2-1; Commanders 2-1.


Last week: Colts beat the Texans 19-17; Commanders beat the Seahawks 33-31.


Last meeting: Commanders beat the Colts 17-16 on Oct. 30, 2022, in Indianapolis.


Series record: Colts lead 21-11.


Matchup to watch
Colts RB Jonathan Taylor vs. the Washington defensive front. Taylor had one of the greatest international performances in league history last season, rushing for 244 yards and three touchdowns, including the game winner in overtime, as Indianapolis beat Atlanta 31-25. The Commanders did a solid job against the Seattle backfield last week.


Stats and stuff
— If Jones and Mariota start, they'd become the seventh and eighth quarterbacks to start an international game in back-to-back seasons in different markets. The others are Matthew Stafford (London 2025, Australia 2026), Aaron Rodgers (London 2024, Ireland 2025), Philip Rivers (London 2018, Mexico 2019), Derek Carr (Mexico 2017, London 2018), Matt Ryan (Canada 2013, London 2014) and Jay Cutler (Canada 2010, London 2011).


— The Colts have 15 penalties, tied for the fewest in the NFL so far.


— Indianapolis has gone 30 consecutive games without a red zone giveaway, the longest active streak in the league.


— Indy's Keenan Allen needs two catches to tie former Colts star Reggie Wayne (1,070) for 11th on the career list.


— The Commanders were the first 0-2 team to defeat the defending Super Bowl champions in Week 3 since 1980, when the Bengals beat the Steelers.


— Washington rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was the NFC defensive player of the week after he had five tackles, two passes defensed and an interception against Seattle. He's Washington's first rookie LB to win the award since Brian Orakpo in Week 14 of 2009.

stories.headline: Diamondbacks retaining Torey Lovullo as manager
stories.summary: Torey Lovullo, the winningest manager in Diamondbacks history over his 10 seasons, is returning on a new contract.
stories.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks are bringing back Torey Lovullo, the winningest manager in franchise history, the team announced on Thursday.

Lovullo, 61, whose deal expired after this season, agreed to a two-year contract.

Lovullo's future with the club was in flux after the Diamondbacks missed the playoffs for a third straight year. Arizona was eliminated from postseason contention on the final day of the regular season for the second time in three seasons when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Tampa Bay Rays 7-4 on Sunday.

The D-backs finished with an 86-76 record -- the best in MLB for a team that didn't qualify for October baseball.

"I want to win a world championship with this organization, but I want to be wanted," Lovullo said after the final game of the regular season. "... I'll leave it at that."

He said earlier this month that he thought the Diamondbacks needed to make the playoffs for him and his coaching staff to return next season.

Diamondbacks president Derrick Hall recently said he thinks Lovullo likely did the best managing job of his career this season while Arizona struggled with major injuries and distractions that included the latest bizarre absence of star Ketel Marte in August.

Lovullo has gone 750-768 during a full decade in charge, with the highlight being a surprise World Series appearance in 2023. He is the third-longest-tenured manager in the big leagues behind Tampa Bay's Kevin Cash and Los Angeles Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts.

The affable Lovullo is a popular presence in the organization. He played eight seasons in the big leagues for seven teams in the 1980s and 1990s. He was the bench coach for the Boston Red Sox when they won the World Series in 2013 and played college baseball at UCLA.

"Arizona is my home," Lovullo said after the final game of the season. "I love Arizona, and the people and the fans are spectacular. The group that I work for is amazing. I love being around them every single day, and I don't want that to change."

Lovullo was hired as Arizona's manager four weeks after Hazen took over as general manager, and their tenures are still intertwined. Their Diamondbacks have had the misfortune to be in the National League West with the dominant Dodgers, who have won 13 of the last 14 division titles -- and with the San Diego Padres, who have made the postseason in five of the past seven years during the best stretch in franchise history.

Arizona, however, hasn't been able to snare a wild-card berth despite rosters full of veteran talent and a solid young core, repeatedly falling just short at big moments.

The Diamondbacks started this season with postseason expectations and were in contention throughout the summer, but the team could never quite reach its full potential. Two of the team's main starting pitchers -- Zac Gallen and Merrill Kelly -- struggled and injuries to ace right-hander Corbin Burnes, relievers A.J. Puk and Justin Martinez, and top prospect Jordan Lawlar put a dent in their depth.

Catcher Gabriel Moreno won the NL batting title this season, but other key hitters like Marte, Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo were inconsistent.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Zach Merrett equals Bombers record with seventh best and fairest win
stories.summary: A few days out from trade period, when Hawthorn are expected to recruit Zach Merrett, the Essendon star has won his seventh club best and fairest award.
stories.body:
Zach Merrett's seventh Essendon best and fairest award win is expected to be his last honour at the Bombers.

The former captain joined fellow Essendon greats Dick Reynolds and Bill Hutchison as the only seven-time winners of the AFL club's Crichton Medal at Thursday night's club awards function.

Trade period starts next Monday and Hawthorn will again try to recruit Merrett, a year after Essendon stood firm following the stunning revelation that he wanted to join their bitter rivals in his quest to win a premiership.

The 30-year-old polled 117 votes, while Sam Durham was runner-up on 106 and Archie Roberts third with 77.

Merrett did not address his playing future when he accepted the award. It would be a major surprise if he is not at Hawthorn next year.

"To see my name on an honour roll, the same number of times as those guys, is a real 'pinch-me' moment," Merrett said of Reynolds and Hutchison.

Reynolds' daugher Suzie and Hutchison's son Ray joined Merrett on stage to mark the moment of Bombers history.

Merrett has won five of Essendon's last seven best and fairest awards. He also took out the player-voted McCracken Medal for the fourth-straight season.

The awards night came three days after Essendon announced a massive off-field recruiting coup, landing Sydney premiership coach John Longmire as their head of performance.

New Bombers coach Mark McVeigh, who worked with Longmire at the Swans, officially welcomed Longmire in his speech at the awards dinner.

"John's a bloody winner," McVeigh said.

President Andrew Welsh also thanked sacked coach Brad Scott and his interim replacement Dean Solomon.

Essendon finished bottom with the worst win-loss in club history (2-21). Welsh said while it was a tough season, there were signs of life.

"I'm not disappointed with the year we had in terms of the growth we've had within our playing group," he said..

"You've seen these young men grow throughout the year and it's something we can genuinely build on.

"We are not a club that is simply here to exist, on or off the field.

"We're here to be relevant, we're here to compete and ultimately we're here to win, week after week.

Welsh and McVeigh warned that unpopular decisions were ahead as the Bombers try to return to the top of the ladder.

"Building a club the right way in the modern era takes hard decisions ... look at Brisbane and Freo," Welsh said.

"They did it the hard way, they went through lean years, they built patiently, they stuck together and now they've been rewarded with sustained success.

"There's no gaming the system ... there are no shortcuts, we're doing it the right way."

stories.headline: Lynx's Napheesa Collier unsure of future as free agency looms
stories.summary: Two-time MVP runner-up Napheesa Collier is unsure of her future as she enters free agency, saying she loves Minnesota but hasn't had time to think about what's next.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Napheesa Collier downplayed talk about her future with the Minnesota Lynx on Thursday, saying she's still dealing with the emotions of being the first 1-seed to lose to an 8-seed in WNBA playoff history.

"Honestly, I haven't even thought about [my future]," Collier said during her exit interview after having been swept in two games by the New York Liberty. "We lost less than 48 hours ago and we didn't expect to be here, so I really haven't had any time to decompress or anything like that.

"I can tell you I love it here. I love the organization. I love my team and everything like that, but I just haven't had the time to give that any thought."

Last summer, Collier, after finishing second behind A'ja Wilson in the 2025 MVP race for the second year in a row, rejected a multiyear deal in lieu of a one-year contract and will now be highly coveted entering free agency.

Collier admitted she wasn't at her best this season -- averaging 16.8 points and 6.9 rebounds -- after returning July 22 from multiple offseason ankle surgeries. In three previous seasons from 2023 to 2025, Collier averaged at least 20 points per game and seven rebounds per game, while finishing fourth, second and second in the MVP race, respectively.

"I mean, obviously, it wasn't the level that I expected for myself. I'm proud of the work that I put into getting to that point," Collier said. "My ultimate goal is to get back on the court and ultimately to help my team win a championship. Obviously, we fell short of that, so that's hard. But still proud of what I was able to accomplish and more than anything proud of the team as well. Obviously, I wasn't 100%, but I gave 100% of what I was able to."

Added Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve: "Everybody could see Napheesa Collier wasn't Napheesa Collier."

But Collier remains an anchor for the team and a free agent with a major decision that could alter the franchise and the entire WNBA. Every team in the WNBA would seemingly make room for the five-time All-Star, if she wanted a change of scenery.

Collier was a bridge for the organization after former superstar Maya Moore abruptly left the league in 2018, ending the reign of a Lynx dynasty that had won four WNBA titles. The sixth overall pick in the 2019 draft, Collier gave Reeve a franchise player to build a new team around. That journey peaked in 2024, when the Lynx reached the WNBA Finals, where they lost to the Liberty.

Locally, Collier's noncommittal words about her future have sounded familiar to sports fans who've watched former WNBA star Katie Smith, baseball All-Star David Ortiz, former NBA All-Stars Kevin Love and Kevin Garnett and even an entire franchise -- the NHL's North Stars -- pick greener pastures before winning championships in those new spots.

Collier might be added to that list in the months ahead, depending on her next move.

"I would just say thank you for everything," Collier said when asked what she would tell fans who wonder if she's played her last game in Minneapolis. "Again, I don't know what to say about that [potentially leaving] part, but through this season and all my eight years here, continuously, the fans are ... a huge reason why Minnesota is just so amazing, why it's so hard for other teams to play in Target Center, why we love playing here.

"The fans, through everything, have stuck beside us through the highs and lows, no matter what the outside noise is."

If Collier leaves, Reeve will have to build a new team around another young star. Although Olivia Miles struggled throughout the playoffs, the WNBA Rookie of the Year said she learned about herself through the loss.

"I think it was an interesting year," Miles said. "We started off with weird expectations and then we got really good and then it was like, 'OK, you guys should win.' And then it felt like if we didn't win, it was the end of the world, almost.

"I was just navigating all those expectations. I also started off as a rookie who no one really thought would do what I did. And now I'm in MVP conversations and now I have to play at that level. And it was just a roller-coaster of expectations and emotions throughout the whole year."

Reeve has navigated this crossroads with star players in the past, but she said she's confident Collier understands the benefits of staying in Minnesota.

"[Collier] knows exactly what exists here. [She] knows the care, the love, all the things that have been poured into her. She's well aware of all of that," Reeve said. "This is a decision that is probably more than basketball. And so wherever she lands, it's going to be because she thinks whatever she chooses or wherever she chooses is the right place for her.

"Sometimes you stay and sometimes you go because maybe there is something -- I don't want to say better -- but maybe better for her. And that's something that I respect. She signed a one-year deal for a reason. It wasn't a multiyear deal. Whatever she decides, we're both going to be OK."

stories.headline: Ducks sign Tristan Luneau to $43.2M extension after 14 NHL games
stories.summary: The Ducks have signed defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year contract extension worth $43.2 million after just 14 career NHL appearances.
stories.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. -- The Anaheim Ducks have signed promising young defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year contract extension worth $43.2 million after just 14 NHL appearances.

The Ducks announced the deal Thursday with the 22-year-old Luneau, whose promising career has been slowed by injury. Now healthy and ready for a full-time NHL role, he inked a long-term deal with the team that drafted him in the second round in 2022.

Luneau was the Quebec major junior league's top defenseman in the 2022-23 season and he made the Ducks' roster out of training camp the following fall. He came down with a viral infection that winter while practicing with Canada's national junior team, however, forcing him to miss the rest of the year.

Anaheim took a deliberate approach with Luneau's health for the past two seasons, keeping him with its AHL affiliate in San Diego for most of that time. But the Ducks never wavered in their belief that Luneau will be an above-average defenseman, and they proved it with a long-term contract for a player who suited up in just one game for the NHL club last season.

Luneau will be expected to play a significant role this season for the Ducks, who lost four veteran defensemen -- Jacob Trouba, captain Radko Gudas, John Carlson and Olen Zellweger -- from last season's already mediocre blue line group over the summer.

Anaheim general manager Pat Verbeek moved aggressively to lock up Luneau after being burned repeatedly in restricted free agency over the offseason.

Verbeek spent months failing to reach a deal with center Leo Carlsson, who then signed a $90 million offer sheet with Philadelphia that briefly made him the NHL's highest-paid player before Anaheim matched it. Carlsson is among the best young centers in hockey, but his deal is worth much more than he was expected to get as a restricted free agent -- as is the five-year, $36 million deal given to Pavel Mintyukov by Verbeek after other teams began to sniff around the Russian defenseman in the wake of Carlsson's massive offer sheet.

Verbeek then signed high-scoring forward Cutter Gauthier to a six-year, $81 million extension last month, but the resulting salary cap constraints from Verbeek's summer of misadventure effectively forced the Ducks to waive 22-goal scorer Chris Kreider, damaging their depth.

Luneau will join Jackson LaCombe and Mintyukov as the new core of the Ducks' defense. Rising star LaCombe agreed to an eight-year, $72 million extension a year ago.

Anaheim ended a seven-year playoff drought last spring, advancing to the second round under coach Joel Quenneville. The Ducks open the regular season Friday at Vegas before their home opener Sunday against Florida.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.

Vasseur's job has come under increasing scrutiny over the past month, with reports last week linking ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner to replace him.

The speculation grew so much Ferrari felt the need this week to clarify that Ferrari's corporate leadership has "full confidence" in Vasseur, albeit via a press conference with the team's head of communications and not through a statement from either company CEO Benedetto Vigna or chairman John Elkann.

"Ultimately, it's not a one-man operation," Hamilton said in a passionate defence of his team boss to TV in Malaysia on Thursday. "If you want to point fingers, point them somewhere else. There are lot of people above that also are a part of it.

"So if you want to take something from this message: Fred's in his position, he's not going anywhere and I'm here to stay with him. And I still believe fully in where we're going."

Speaking to the written media afterwards, Hamilton reiterated: "I think Fred has the full backing.

"There often seems to be a lot of focus on one individual in one role here. And you can see that, obviously, they've switched out lots of different people in Fred's role. But Fred is a fantastic leader.

"He really is the guy to take his team in the right direction. However, there is a structure that's been there for some time. Whether or not that needs looking at moving forward, there are obviously also people above Fred, and it's not about one person.

"Fred has led the team to ... He's helped make changes in this past year, he's helped us get to the second in the constructors' championship. That's a huge step from last year."

Hamilton was then asked if one of the issues Ferrari has is that Vasseur has no financial stake in the race team, unlike his former boss Toto Wolff, who oversees all facets of the Mercedes F1 team.

In reply to whether Ferrari could benefit with a similar structure to Mercedes, Hamilton said: "There are changes that I would make, but I'm not going to talk about what those are. Toto's in a different position to Fred. The structure's a lot different. That's all I can say."

Ferrari has always been subjected to intense scrutiny, attention which has likely only increased the longer the team's title drought has gone on -- the team's last constructors' title was 2008, with its last drivers' title in 2007.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Hamilton said the recent reporting about the state of the internals of the team have been wide of the market.

"For me, it's frustrating to see all the negativity. Because you see other people making mistakes, and they don't normally say too much about them," he said.

"We either make the same mistake, or are not perfect and and it's ten times worse for some reason for Ferrari, but that's also to be expected. Given that it's the best brand here, it's the most iconic by far. For me, I don't read a lot, so that has zero effect on me. But of course, when I come into the room and see, it definitely affects individuals on the team.

"Because every weekend they try and show up and do the best job they can, and they don't get it right all the time. Families are messaging you for all the negative things that they're reading when the people back at the factory are reading all those things, even though they're giving their all. It's almost like sometimes you feel like there's nothing you can do right, even when you're giving your all.

"For me, the message is to not read any of the stuff that's being written. Because the fact is, nobody that's writing any of the stuff has actually any clue what they're talking about, because they're not in the team.

"They don't know what's happening behind closed doors. They don't know how hard everybody's working. It's all down to assumptions and opinions."

Vasseur and Hamilton worked together back in Formula 2 before being reunited at Ferrari.

"Fred's been fantastic working with me and I think our relationship as a whole -- even with our bosses -- is in a better place than it ever was," he added to television.

"Fred's made a lot of changes I've asked for already. I think it's not an easy time for Fred so I think it's good that the team came out with that earlier this week. I've also let him know I support him 100%.

"I wouldn't be here without Fred. Swapping him out ... it won't change how the team moves forwards. It would be detrimental to it."

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: Roosters star admits he is torn on World Cup decision
stories.summary: Robert Toia has revealed he is still undecided if he wants to play for Australia or Tonga in the World Cup, less than a week out from teams being named.
stories.body:
Robert Toia has admitted he still doesn't know who he wants to play for at the World Cup, as the in-demand centre weighs up representing Tonga or Australia.

Toia is the highest-profile player caught in a tug-of-war between nations, with the World Cup just a fortnight ago and final squads to be announced next week.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf had told AAP this week that Toia had indicated he wanted to represent the Pacific nation, after debuting for them last year.

Australia counterpart Kevin Walters has also made clear he believes the Sydney Roosters star is available for the Kangaroos, and he has not been told otherwise.

Toia has accepted he must make a decision soon, but remains uncertain what way he will go with Sunday's NRL grand final against Newcastle before this month's tournament.

"To be honest, I have not made my mind up," Toia told AAP.

"I just find it hard that I don't have a decision. I want to play for Tonga, it means so much to my family, myself and my people.

"I went over to Tonga last year and you can see how much it means to them.

"But to have Australia on your resume. Just to play for Australia, in my second year, I find it such a massive achievement. That's what I'm kind of weighing up."

Beyond Toia, Woolf also believes Sydney Roosters teammates Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong want to play for Tonga in the global showpiece.

Queensland winger Jojo Fifita revealed this week he too was still undecided, weighing up whether to play for Australia, New Zealand or Tonga.

Fifita told AAP he'd had discussions with all three nations, although he was not named in the Kiwis' initial 40-man squad.

Walters has said both Jojo and his brother David are under consideration for Australia's World Cup squad.

In better news for Tonga, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has confirmed he will be fit for the tournament after a syndesmosis injury in the preliminary-final loss to the Roosters.

"I don't need surgery. I will be able to play in the World Cup," Katoa said.

"I immediately knew I had done something, so I was definitely happy once I got the scans back it wasn't too bad and I will be able to represent Tonga."

Complicating matters for players who are weighing up their future is the fact Australian representatives stand to earn $40,000 by playing in the tournament.

AAP is aware of coaches and players who are concerned that may prompt some players to choose the Kangaroos in order to benefit their families.

But Katoa said it would never be a factor for him.

"I'd never look at the price tag, it's always where my heart is at," he said.

"I've always said my heart is at Tonga and if it wasn't for Tonga I am half-Cook Islands as well. So if it wasn't for Tonga, I would go Cook Islands."

Meanwhile it is understood Tonga will pick former St George Illawarra half Talatau Amone in their squad for the tournament.

Amone has not played since he was deregistered by the NRL in 2023 for assault. Tonga are still yet to learn if he will be cleared to play in the tournament.

He can return to the NRL next year, and starred on his return to Queensland Cup with Wynnum-Manly in recent months.
